unit.why: A quoted excerpt in which R. Gershon of Kuty's remark to the Besht on prayer is followed by R. Nahman's eyewitness account of the Besht's face changing colour, like fire and then like snow, while he prayed.
unit.boundary_note: part of a chain of quotations from Hasidic books on prayer; the previous and next divisions are separate excerpts

stories.start_quote: ובס׳ ה״ה (פ׳ תצא) וז״ל כמו שאמר
stories.end_quote: וברגע כשלג בכל רגע לגוון אחר
stories.summary_en: R. Gershon of Kuty tells his brother-in-law the Besht, before he recognized the Besht's rank, that true prayer means the soul leaving the body, and R. Nahman testifies that as a youth he crept under the Besht's tallit during prayer and saw his face turn, moment by moment, from a burning torch to snow and to other colours.
